# Wire baseline fixtures

These baseline snapshots are independent of the session request encoder. They
were captured with bincode 2.0.1 standard serde encoding directly from the wire
declarations,
without `session`, `wire::request`, or the bounded encoder. Expected bytes are
checked in, never generated by the tests.

The release source is tag `0.21.0`; the source inspected when this PR was
created is
`78cbfff4fc963c81cebf24326090f7dcbdb4498d` (crate `0.22.0`). The relevant
`AgentInfo`/base/tail source is retained in `protocol-0.21.0-lib.txt`. Request-code
assignments from that tag are in `agent-request-codes.txt` and
`server-request-codes.txt`. These declarations and assignments are unchanged in
that inspected source, so both sets of binary snapshots are identical.
The protocol constants in both are `0.49.0` and `>=0.49.0`.

The session foundation now builds on `0.24.0`. The captured handshake and
response values remain unchanged. The request-code tests also pin the engine
commands (23–26) and reports (41–44) added in `0.23.0`; transport tests carry
`0.24.0` install requests with a selected privilege profile. These additions do
not change the historical snapshots.

The captured values are:

- Base handshake: agent name `agent`, agent version `1.2.3`, protocol version
  `0.49.0`, IPv4 address `127.0.0.1:8080`, status `Ready`.
- Complete handshake: that base, capabilities `node.package` and `registrar` in
  sorted order, active trust epoch `Some(42)`, manifest format range
  `Some({min: 1, max: 2})`, no provisioning fingerprint, no audit health.
- Power response: `Ok(NodePowerResponse::Initiated)`.
- Install preflight: `Ok(InstallPreflight::UnknownConfigTemplate {id: "custom"})`.
- Remote text: `Err("not supported")`, with unit success type.

Base bytes were encoded independently as a five-field tuple. Complete bytes used
the existing derived `AgentInfo::Serialize`. Responses used the existing typed
wire enums. The fixtures contain payload bytes only. Tests separately pin the
big-endian frame header, all little-endian fixed-width request codes, and standard
bincode integer bytes (`300_u32` is `fb 2c 01`, not a fixed-width body).

A tail ending before an entire optional field is valid; a present `Some` marker
without its value is malformed. Tests distinguish those cases and compare the
legacy and guarded decoders against these same fixtures.
